name: httpx timeouts, retries, and shared AsyncClient lifecycle
short_definition: Outbound HTTP from Python services uses httpx as the default client (sync Client + async AsyncClient). Own one shared AsyncClient in FastAPI lifespan for connection pooling; set explicit connect/read/write/pool timeouts (default is 5s network inactivity); retry only idempotent methods with bounded backoff; never follow user-controlled redirects into private networks. As of 2026-07-13 PyPI: httpx 0.28.1, httpcore 1.0.9, tenacity 9.1.4, httpx-retries 0.6.0, hishel 1.3.0.
scope_in: httpx.AsyncClient / Client configuration (timeouts, Limits, HTTP/2, proxies)
Shared client lifecycle via FastAPI lifespan or dependency
Retry policy for idempotent requests (transport retries vs tenacity/httpx-retries)
Outbound SSRF-adjacent hardening for server-side fetch (allowlists, no open proxy)
When requests/aiohttp still appear and what to migrate
scope_out: LLM provider SDKs internals (use their client if required; still set timeouts)
Browser fetch / Next.js BFF outbound (typescript path)
Full SSRF product design details beyond HTTP client knobs (py-auth-security)

defaults.client: httpx.AsyncClient shared for service lifetime; close on shutdown
defaults.timeout: httpx.Timeout(connect=5.0, read=30.0, write=10.0, pool=5.0) — tune per upstream; never timeout=None in prod
defaults.limits: httpx.Limits(max_connections=100, max_keepalive_connections=20) default-ish; lower for scarce upstreams
defaults.retries: Only GET/HEAD/OPTIONS (and PUT with idempotency key); exponential backoff + jitter; respect Retry-After on 429
defaults.retry_impl: Prefer tenacity or httpx-retries over bare loops; AsyncHTTPTransport(retries=N) is connection-error only, not status codes
defaults.http2: http2=True only when upstream benefits and h2 extra installed; not default everywhere
defaults.follow_redirects: False by default for security-sensitive fetches; if True, cap max redirects and validate final host
defaults.verify: TLS verify on; system trust via certifi/truststore; never verify=False in prod
defaults.per_request: Override timeout per call for slow AI providers vs internal APIs

use_httpx_when: Any new Python service needs outbound HTTP (sync or async)
Need HTTP/2, streaming responses, or typed timeouts
do_not_use_when: In-process ASGI call without HTTP — prefer direct function/DI, not loopback HTTP
Vendor SDK that owns its own transport and forbids replacement without cause

alternatives.requests: Legacy sync only; do not greenfield; migrate to httpx
alternatives.aiohttp: Acceptable if already deep in aiohttp stack; otherwise httpx for unified sync/async API
alternatives.hishel: HTTP cache layer on httpx for RFC-aware response caching
alternatives.rust_reqwest: Hand off ultra-hot proxy paths to Rust when measured

do: Create AsyncClient once in lifespan; inject via app.state or Depends
Set granular Timeout; log TimeoutException with upstream name
Raise_for_status or map status codes explicitly; never ignore 4xx/5xx silently
Retry budget: max 2–3 attempts, only idempotent, with jitter
Propagate X-Request-Id / trace context headers outbound
Mock with respx or pytest-httpx in unit tests; real HTTP only in contract tests
dont: Don't httpx.get() top-level per request in hot paths (no pool reuse)
Don't timeout=None or multi-minute defaults without product reason
Don't retry POST/PATCH without idempotency key (double charge / double create)
Don't follow redirects to user-supplied URLs without host allowlist
Don't disable SSL verify to 'fix' local cert issues in committed code
Don't share one Client across event loops / threads carelessly

code_skeleton:
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated

import httpx
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException

DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = httpx.Timeout(connect=5.0, read=30.0, write=10.0, pool=5.0)
DEFAULT_LIMITS = httpx.Limits(max_connections=100, max_keepalive_connections=20)

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    app.state.http = httpx.AsyncClient(
        timeout=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT,
        limits=DEFAULT_LIMITS,
        headers={"User-Agent": "myservice/1.0"},
        follow_redirects=False,
    )
    yield
    await app.state.http.aclose()

app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)

async def get_http() -> httpx.AsyncClient:
    return app.state.http

HttpClient = Annotated[httpx.AsyncClient, Depends(get_http)]

@app.get("/proxy-health")
async def proxy_health(http: HttpClient) -> dict[str, str]:
    try:
        r = await http.get("https://example.com/health", timeout=httpx.Timeout(5.0))
        r.raise_for_status()
    except httpx.TimeoutException as e:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=504, detail="upstream timeout") from e
    except httpx.HTTPError as e:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=502, detail="upstream error") from e
    return {"upstream": "ok"}
failure_modes: Per-request Client() → connection exhaustion / TIME_WAIT storms under load
Default 5s read timeout kills legitimate slow LLM/provider calls without per-route override
timeout=None hangs workers forever on black-hole upstreams
Retries on non-idempotent POST amplify outages and double side effects
PoolTimeout under fan-out (many concurrent upstreams) misdiagnosed as app hang
SSRF via user URL + follow_redirects into 169.254.169.254 / RFC1918
Client not closed on reload/shutdown → FD leaks in dev
anti_patterns: import requests in new FastAPI services
Bare except: pass around httpx errors
Hardcoded secrets in Authorization headers in repo
Global module-level AsyncClient created at import without test override
Retry forever / while True without budget
verify=False committed to fix corporate proxy MITM

config_snippets.tenacity_get:
from tenacity import retry, stop_after_attempt, wait_exponential_jitter, retry_if_exception_type
import httpx

@retry(
    reraise=True,
    stop=stop_after_attempt(3),
    wait=wait_exponential_jitter(initial=0.2, max=2.0),
    retry=retry_if_exception_type((httpx.TransportError, httpx.TimeoutException)),
)
async def get_idempotent(client: httpx.AsyncClient, url: str) -> httpx.Response:
    r = await client.get(url)
    if r.status_code in {502, 503, 504}:
        r.raise_for_status()  # trigger retry via custom or wrap
    return r

deprecation_watch: requests as default in new services
Unbounded urllib3 Retry copied into async code
aiohttp session per request without connector limits
ts_boundary: Next.js Route Handlers / Server Actions use fetch with AbortSignal timeouts. Python httpx is for Python services calling third parties, LLM gateways, or internal APIs. Do not proxy browser secrets through Python without auth; prefer same OpenAPI contracts. When Next BFF already has the token cookie session, call Python with service JWT or forwarded user JWT per boundary design.
rust_boundary: Move to reqwest/Axum when outbound fan-out or proxy volume is CPU/latency critical, or when you need a pure edge proxy. Keep httpx for app-level integration and AI glue where developer velocity matters.
supabase_boundary: Prefer supabase-py or direct PostgREST with service role only on server; set short timeouts on Auth/REST admin calls. Never point open httpx at user-supplied Supabase URLs. Storage signed URL fetch still needs size limits and content-type checks.
boundary_contracts: Document per-upstream timeout SLOs in runbooks
Map upstream 429 → client 429 or 503 with Retry-After policy
OpenAPI not required for pure egress clients; still version internal APIs

decision_matrix_row.problem_class: Service needs outbound HTTP to APIs/providers
decision_matrix_row.ts: fetch + AbortSignal in Next server; undici defaults

threats: SSRF via user-controlled URL, redirects, DNS rebinding
Credential leakage in logs (Authorization, Set-Cookie mirrored)
Retry amplification / accidental DoS of upstream
Open proxy misuse of internal httpx client
mitigations: Allowlist hosts/schemes (https only); block link-local and private ranges unless explicit
Redact auth headers in structured logs
Retry caps + circuit breaker for unhealthy upstreams
verify TLS; pin corporate CA via truststore when required
Separate clients for trusted internal vs untrusted user-driven fetch

must_generate: Shared AsyncClient in lifespan with aclose()
Retries only on idempotent methods with stop condition
must_not_generate: retry on all methods including POST without idempotency
New Client() inside every request handler

tests_required: Retry count on transport error (assert call count)
No retry on POST without key
Client closed after lifespan / fixture teardown
respx route for happy path JSON
SSRF unit test: private IP rejected when allowlist enforced
ci_gates: grep/scan: no verify=False, no timeout=None in app code

positive: await client.aclose() or async with AsyncClient
negative: while True: await client.get without break/budget

skill_module_bullets: One AsyncClient per app lifetime; never per-request in hot paths
Always set Timeout(connect/read/write/pool); default 5s is not 'no timeout'
Retries: idempotent only, budgeted, prefer tenacity/httpx-retries
AsyncHTTPTransport(retries=N) ≠ full HTTP status retry policy
Test with respx; ban verify=False and timeout=None in prod code
action_items: Scan rules: requests import, verify=False, timeout=None
Sample lifespan client in skill samples
checklist: Timeouts per upstream class (internal vs AI)
HTTP/2 only if needed + h2 installed
conflicts_noted: AsyncHTTPTransport(retries=) only covers certain connection failures; community often confuses it with status-code retries
Some guides still push aiohttp as the async default; httpx is preferred here for API symmetry and FastAPI test story
httpx-retries vs tenacity: both fine; pick one style per repo
